 Eagles injury update: Saquon Barkley set to play against Commanders 
 Eagles running back Saquon Barkley returned to practice on Friday afternoon and will play on Sunday. 
 By Dave Zangaro • 
 Published October 30, 2026 • 
 Updated on October 30, 2026 at 4:16 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion spoke to the media on Thursday and was asked about the progress he’s seen from rookie tackle Markel Bell this season. 
 Saquon Barkley is good to go against the Commanders on Sunday night.
 After missing the first two days of the week, Barkley returned to practice on Friday afternoon and does not have a game status entering this game. He's expected to play.
 Barkley (hamstring/back) said he will need to manage his injuries throughout the course of the game with a plan set forth from the Eagles’ training staff. Basically, he doesn’t want his body to lock up.
 "One day, I’m not going to be playing football," Barkley said. "Whenever that is and I look back, I don’t want to look back and be like, ‘I could have gave it a chance and I didn’t.’ Kind of what I live by. So I’m going to just keep recovering, being smart. But I like playing football. If I have the opportunity to play, I’m going to try my best to play."
 Here's the final injury report of the week:
 Out: DeVonta Smith (hamstring), Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad), Britain Covey (knee), Jonathan Jones (hamstring)
 Questionable: Jakorian Bennett (knee)

 Barkley (hamstring/back) played through injuries in the 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night. Despite being nowhere near 100 percent, Barkley still played well on Monday, rushing for 62 yards and a touchdown on 7 carries and catching 2 passes for 9 yards.
 “We’ll see at the end of this,” head coach Nick Sirianni said about Barkley on Friday morning. “And so guys are having a good week of preparation. Feel good about that room. Obviously, we’ve been beat up in that room with injuries. But I feel good about the depth and the guys that we have. 
 “I was really excited about Elijah throughout camp and then he got dinged up in camp and just really glad to have him back. And always have liked Jaydon and the things he can do going back to watching him coming out of Texas. Feel good about that room. Obviously, a little beat up in that room and looking forward to when we can get guys back. But I’m excited about these guys that are going to go out there and rip it.”
 Without Smith, Wicks and Covey, the Eagles’ receivers for this game will be Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Elijah Moore and Hollywood Brown. Lemon seems likely to take over punt returner duties.
 Nolan Smith was a full participant in Friday's practice and will make his return against the Commanders after missing the Cowboys game.
